{"concern":"core","designation":"internal","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"A cluster can be declared deliberately separate, so disconnected_community reports undeclared islands instead of one permanent warning","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"A group of nodes can be declared a DELIBERATE PARTITION — a subsystem that genuinely does not couple to the rest of the design — so `disconnected_community` reports "N declared partitions, 0 undeclared" rather than one standing warning. The value is NOT silencing the finding. It is that a NEW accidental island becomes visible against the declared ones, which today it is not.

THE DEFECT IN THE CURRENT BEHAVIOUR IS THE SUGGESTED FIX, not the finding. `disconnected_community` proposes `generate_bridge` — creating edges to connect the cluster. Where the separation is correct, acting on that suggestion FABRICATES RELATIONSHIPS THAT DO NOT EXIST in order to silence a warning about a separation that is right. That is manufacturing connectivity, and it is the same act as formatting coverage into existence — with the difference that here THE TOOL PROPOSES IT.

WHY ACKNOWLEDGEMENT IS NOT ENOUGH, which is the part that makes this a mechanism and not a workflow note: `acknowledge_defect` is a one-time answer to a finding whose SIZE keeps changing. Acknowledged at 88 nodes it now reads 121 — at what point is it a different finding? And an alarm that can never be cleared is one everyone learns to skip, so the real disconnection arrives inside a warning nobody reads.

REFLOW2 HAS ALREADY MET THIS AND WROTE DOWN THE ANSWER, which is the strongest evidence that the shape is right. dec:documentation-has-no-operational-coupling (ACCEPTED, 2026-07-24) records the identical situation — three bridges attempted, all refused as lies, the island accepted — and concludes "flagging it is a false positive of the BL-84 family, and THE FIX BELONGS IN THE DETECTOR RATHER THAN IN THE DESIGN." It also states the exact constraint storyflow independently arrived at sixteen days later: "the exemption must not be written in a way that hides a genuine disconnection." The detector fix was never built, because that particular island dissolved on its own when a capability turned out to belong to two components.

REPRODUCED IN THIS DESIGN, 2026-08-09, WITHIN THE HOUR OF THE REPORT ARRIVING: capturing four governance requirements under dec:governance-integrates-not-splits produced heal:33d1548dae64e97a — "5 nodes form a cluster disconnected from the rest of the design", suggested_fix_type `generate_bridge`. No honest bridge existed, so none was drawn. Storyflow hit it at 121 nodes; reflow2 hit it at 5. Both clusters are GOVERNANCE, and both GROW as governance is properly captured — so the detector currently penalises exactly the work dec:governance-integrates-not-splits committed to.

Their stated bound: the growth from 88 to 121 is suggestive, not proven, because the two measurements may not share a scope.
